app.browser.tunnel-not-open: Cannot start: enable the Port Forwarding app first

app.browser.tunnel-no-window: Cannot open a window for the Port Forwarding app
app.browser.tunnel-needs-window: The tunnel API declares that it needs a window; please update the Port Forwarding app
app.browser.tunnel-timeout: Timed out while starting the Port Forwarding app
app.browser.tunnel-bad-args: The Port Forwarding app rejected the arguments:
app.browser.proxy-ready-browser-not: The proxy is ready but the browser did not open
app.browser.invalid-address: Enter a valid address, such as 8080 or 192.168.100.1:80
app.browser.browser-not-open-proxy-ready: The browser did not open, but the SOCKS5 proxy is ready
app.browser.proxy-hint: Point your browser's SOCKS5 proxy at the address above to reach the host's intranet through the local tunnel.
app.browser.not-in-list: The selected browser is not in the detected list; read the list again
app.browser.proxy-required: A proxy is required, e.g. socks5://127.0.0.1:10801
app.browser.browser-list-failed: Failed to read the browser list: {v1}
app.browser.launch-died: The browser exited immediately after starting; this machine may have no graphical session
app.browser.warn-safari-proxy: Safari launched, but Safari does not accept a command-line proxy argument, so the SOCKS5 tunnel was not applied
app.browser.error-write-profile: Failed to write the browser profile: {v1}
app.browser.no-browser-linux: No browser detected. On Debian/Ubuntu install chromium or microsoft-edge-stable; on Arch install chromium; or set QXSSH_BROWSER to an executable path.
app.browser.no-browser-mac: No browser detected. Install one with Homebrew: brew install --cask chromium. The built-in Safari is also usable (it takes no proxy argument, so set the proxy inside the browser).
app.browser.no-browser-win: No browser detected. Install Chrome, Edge, or Firefox, or set QXSSH_BROWSER to an executable path.
app.browser.api-open-desc: Open an address in the browser: { url, mode?: 'socks'|'iframe' }. socks launches the system browser through a tunnel, iframe uses the embedded reverse proxy; returns { mode, proxy, url }. Requires term:open.
